newsitem.title: USA: Ohio treasurer says eyeing new debt policy.
newsitem.headline: Ohio treasurer says eyeing new debt policy.

text.p: - Ohio Treasurer J. Kenneth Blackwell said Wednesday that a new, comprehensive debt management policy was on the agenda for his office.

Blackwell, speaking at the Bond Buyer's Midwest Public Finance Conference in Chicago, said the new policy would be used to assist the state in reviewing its current balance between appropriation and general obligation debt.
He added that the review would include the use of commercial paper and variable-rate bonds.
"The end result is better service and lower costs to the state, and better service to the taxpayer," Blackwell said.
He also said a request for proposals for a financial adviser was recently sent out.
The Republican treasurer also reiterated his long-time warning against derivatives, predicting that "another wave" of problems will come.

Last year, Blackwell spearheaded the passage of an Ohio law prohibiting local governments' use of derivatives in the wake of investment problems experienced by numerous municipalities, school districts and counties in Ohio.
Blackwell pointed out that in addition to safeguards in the law, 732 public funds managers have attended investment training courses.
